reason: Reviewed all five surfaces for attending a Codex thread whose hooks never ran, and for telling its agent once. Lifecycle hooks: no hook definition or output changes. A send from a Codex thread names its CODEX_HOME, working directory and originator override in the hub's notified hint, and repeats that hint on later sends while no hub reports the thread running; the hub then attends a thread it does not hold, without a Session Child, while a live Codex process holds the thread's writer lock in a place that receives, and a thread it holds without a child runs again on such a hint. Such a thread reports accepts_messages false, so it takes no notes until a hook brings a child. Older hubs ignore the new hint fields; older CLIs send none. Updated CLI guidance: the first send from a Codex thread whose Notifai handlers are new, changed or off in its Codex home prints one stderr line (claimed once per thread by a sessions/<id>.hooks-notice marker) telling the agent to carry on and end its reply with the Codex hooks reminder as written. The reminder (also doctor's and a refused ask's user_action.message) now names the home when Codex runs in a home other than ~/.codex under a host Notifai cannot identify, such as T3 Code or Orca: run `CODEX_HOME=<home> codex` in a terminal, then /hooks; the Codex CLI, app and editor keep their existing wording, since their own step already approves the home they run in. Notifai skill and harness setup: the Codex reference already says to carry on and end the reply with the gap's message as written, and that a distinct CODEX_HOME needs its own /hooks approval, so it needs no edit. CLI readiness: doctor, init and status output are unchanged apart from that user_action wording; hooks-trust still reports the unapproved handlers. hub.session gains an attended-unhooked event; the diagnostics reference's description of hub.session stays accurate. Domain terms: unchanged. skills/guidance-changes.json carries one release note for this change.
